items.summary: Singapore expressed strong disappointment with proposed U.S. tariffs, arguing the United States Trade Representative (USTR) failed to account for its open, trade-reliant economic structure. In a November 26 statement, the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry said Singapore 'disagrees with the USTR's findings,' following the agency's November 25 proposal under Section 301 to impose tariffs of up to 20% on Singapore alongside 13 other trading partners for producing more goods than market conditions would warrant. The duties could take effect in early 2027, though USTR Jamieson Greer offered to consider lowering the rate to 10% if Singapore reaches an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with Washington. METI said it will continue constructive engagement and submit further comments during a January public consultation period. The proposed tariffs follow a 168-page investigation report citing structural excess capacity linked to Singapore's Manufacturing 2030 plan, Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 plan, financial support for manufacturing firms in electronics, semiconductors, health, and petrochemicals industries, and encouragement of foreign direct investment from non-market economies such as China. METI countered that the USTR findings ignore Singapore's outward- and market-oriented economy, its role as a trusted trading hub, and asserted that its free trade agreements comply with World Trade Organization rules without protecting domestic markets or subsidizing export manufacturing. The ministry pointed to the US-Singapore Free Trade Agreement under which both sides levy no tariffs on each other's goods; since signing, the U.S. has run a consistent trade surplus for more than 20 years, reaching US$27 billion (S$34.8 billion) in 2024 and growing to US$33 billion in 2025.
items.title: Singapore Disappointed by Proposed US Tariffs Overlook of Its Trade-Reliant Economy

items.summary: On Nov 25, the Trump administration announced a plan to raise tariffs on China (to 20%), Vietnam (18% if a trade pact is finalized), Bangladesh/Cambodia/Indonesia/Malaysia/Thailand (18%), India (17% if a deal completes), and several others at rates from 10% to 15%, citing 'structural excess capacity' in foreign manufacturing. The new levies will not stack on existing July duties of 10% or 12.5% applied to about 60 economies, with only the higher rate applying where both sets overlap; oil/gas and certain food products would be exempted. The plan could be implemented as early as January after a public comment process. Legally, Trump shifted from Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 (a time-limited flat 10% levy) to Section 301, which allows unlimited-rate tariffs in response to trade measures deemed discriminatory but requires investigation before rollout. Studies by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and others show tariffs have raised consumer prices and hurt economic output; the Tax Foundation estimates Trump's tariffs increased taxes by an average of US$1,000 per household in 2025 (before the Supreme Court ruling) and projects US$820 per household in 2026, while forecasting a 0.4% reduction in long-term economic capacity. Tariffs contributed to Democrats winning midterm control of Congress amid voter anger over prices; two-thirds of exit-poll voters said tariffs hurt the economy. Despite signs of manufacturing recovery, economists say higher costs and policy uncertainty have chilled hiring and investment.
items.title: Trump's New Tariff Plan and Its Economic Impact

items.summary: Elon Musk has pledged to give every currently active Trump Account in the United States two shares of SpaceX — one newly issued share from the company and a matching personal share from himself — valuing the total gift at almost $18 billion. The pledge was announced on X, where Musk said the company's shares would be transferred next month while his own would follow once his lockup expires in June 2026; SpaceX did not immediately comment on whether its donations are linked to Trump accounts. The valuation reflects SpaceX shares closing at $127.44 and is tied to a program that has opened almost 70 million accounts for Americans under 18, with the White House reporting nearly 70 million accounts last month. This follows an October pledge in which Musk announced giving one of his own SpaceX shares — he held about 6.42 billion as of June — to every child in America; most of his philanthropy reportedly flows through the Musk Foundation's roughly $16bn in assets, and separately Gwynne Shotwell and her husband pledged a share each to more than 2 million children under the initiative. The article contrasts this with Anthropic's approach after its recent IPO: committing 5% of shares to a public-good fund worth around $54bn at current prices — sharply different from Musk's per-child distribution. It also notes other long-running philanthropy, including Warren Buffett reportedly having given away $60bn toward his roughly $150bn fortune and the Gates Foundation distributing more than $100bn since its 2000 founding.
items.title: Elon Musk Pledges Two SpaceX Shares to Every US Child, Valuing the Gift at Nearly $18bn

items.summary: NVIDIA announced enhancements to its open-source document model Nemotron 3.5 Parse, which converts page images into structured data (reading order, content classes such as headings/paragraphs/tables/charts, and bounding boxes) for retrieval-augmented generation and agents. The update adds three open-sourced synthetic training datasets—Synthetic Charts V1 with 9.98M examples, Synthetic Tables V1 with 1M examples, and OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 with 7.9M examples—to support chart/table reading (including inferring values from unmarked charts) and multilingual OCR. NVIDIA also released a fine-tuning recipe using supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards via Group Relative Policy Optimization; in its dental-form reference run, the estimated first-attempt success rate rose from 0.00% for the base model to 95.85% after SFT and 96.58% after RLVR on held-out forms. A matched comparison of supervised fine-tuning versus GRPO checkpoints showed loop-flagged outputs falling from 126 to 29 pages (about 77% fewer), outputs hitting the 9,000-token limit dropping from 185 to 35, and an overall score improving from 66.24 to 71.38 (+5.18 tables, +4.15 charts). For faster inference, NVIDIA introduced a DFlash2 speculator that proposes up to 32 tokens ahead (averaging about 14 accepted draft tokens per verification step), which in native single-pass benchmarking on one H200 raised throughput 7.62× at concurrency 1 and 1.52× at concurrency 512 versus Parse 3.5 with speculation disabled.
items.title: NVIDIA Open-Sources Synthetic Datasets, Fine-Tuning Recipe, and DFlash2 Speculator for Nemotron 3.5 Parse

items.summary: The article explains that sqlite3_rsync, an experimental tool added to SQLite in version 3.47.0 (October 2024) and enhanced in 3.50.0 (May 2025), lets users copy or synchronize a snapshot of a database over SSH without first creating a full local duplicate. Normally obtaining such a snapshot requires either the backup API or VACUUM INTO, both of which demand enough disk space to hold an entire second copy—so instances already using more than half their available disk cannot do so at all. sqlite3_rsync instead works like regular rsync: the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages to the origin side, and the origin returns differing page content or requests finer-grained hashes when a multi-page hash does not match. The author notes that if the two sides start out vastly different, total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database due to hash-exchange overhead, though this excess is small—a few percent at most.
items.title: sqlite3_rsync Enables Remote SQLite Snapshots Without a Local Duplicate

items.summary: On November 23, Nvidia reinstated cofounder Jensen Huang as president and CEO less than two weeks after his abrupt resignation triggered a leadership crisis. The board said it consulted senior U.S. government officials before the return and concluded it posed no national security risk, though its investigation remains open and Nvidia announced additional measures to address national security and compliance concerns. Analyst Andy Thurai of The Field CTO argued Huang's departure raised questions about Nvidia's institutional maturity, noting that companies like Apple and IBM spend years preparing successor leaders—distinguishing a mature corporate entity from a founder-led company—and concluded Nvidia still needs to prepare for a future without him. Separately, Anthropic went public on November 19 at an IPO price of $83 per share, described as one of the largest initial public offerings in history; according to data from Hill.com reported by CNN, about 96% of its estimated employees held equity worth more than $1 million at that price. On its first trading day Anthropic's stock opened at $111.50 before closing at $97.17, meaning investors who bought at the IPO price profited while those who bought when trading opened were already underwater. Both events coincide with continued billions of dollars flowing into AI, prompting Hetz Ventures managing partner Judah Taub to argue that investors should separate their enthusiasm for AI from an assessment of what these companies are actually making.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Amid AI IPO and Financing Debate

items.summary: Noida Power Co. Ltd. (NPCL) concluded its 300 MW round-the-clock (RTC) renewable energy tender, awarding 85 MW to ReNew at INR 4.43 ($0.048)/kWh and 215 MW to Purvah Green Power at INR 4.44/kWh. The tender procured RTC power from interstate transmission system (ISTS)-connected renewable projects integrated with energy storage systems through tariff-based competitive bidding, on a build-own-operate basis under 25-year power purchase agreements. Developers must supply at least 50% of contracted capacity in each time block outside peak hours and at least 90% during peak hours throughout the PPA period (q10: 50%, q11: 90%). Selected developers may sell surplus electricity to third parties or through power exchanges without a no-objection certificate from NPCL. For context, in October 2018 UPNEDA launched a 550 MW solar tender earmarking 50 MW for NPCL under a 25-year PPA with a tariff ceiling of INR 3.10/kWh (q13: 550 MW, q14: 50 MW, q15: 3.10). In August 2026 SECI concluded its 1 GW RTC tender at tariffs ranging from INR 5.25/kWh to INR 5.26/kWh (q17: 1 GW, q18: 5.25, q19: 5.26), and in November 2025 Railway Energy Management Co. Ltd. awarded 1 GW of RTC capacity at INR 4.35/kWh with ReNew and Purvah Green Power securing 200 MW and 180 MW respectively (q21: 1 GW, q22: 4.35, q23: 200 MW, q24: 180 MW).
items.title: Indian utility's round-the-clock renewables tender yields tariffs from $0.048/kWh

items.summary: Researchers at Spain's University of Burgos developed and tested a full-size photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) collector featuring an embedded heat-storage layer combining paraffin, which stores heat as it melts, with expanded graphite that increases the paraffin's thermal conductivity more than 30-fold. The prototype used a commercial 200 W monocrystalline PERC module measuring 1,500 mm × 676 mm, behind which they arranged 18 expanded-graphite tiles impregnated with Rubitherm RT44HC paraffin in three columns and six rows. The 20 mm-thick tiles weighed a total of 15.7 kg and contained 9% expanded graphite by mass.
items.title: Spanish researchers build photovoltaic-thermal prototype with graphite-paraffin heat storage

items.summary: Juniper Green Energy Limited signed a 150 MW hybrid renewable energy Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with NTPC Limited through its wholly owned subsidiary Juniper Green Gem Private Limited. The agreement has raised the company's total contracted renewable energy capacity to approximately 6.4 GWp, and it also holds a contracted Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity of 4.3 GWh. Of that portfolio, about 3 GWp of renewable energy capacity and 700 MWh of battery storage are currently operational. The PPA runs for 25 years from the Scheduled Commencement of Supply Date, and the project is scheduled to reach commercial operation by June 2028. Ankush Malik, Whole-time Director and CEO of Juniper Green Energy, said the hybrid configuration aims to deliver more predictable power during peak demand hours.
items.title: Juniper Green Energy Signs 150 MW Hybrid Renewable PPA With NTPC, Expands Portfolio To 6.4 GWp

items.summary: Moglix has launched Moglix Solar, an end-to-end rooftop solar business aimed at industrial, commercial, and residential customers in India. The new business will leverage Moglix's industrial supply chain expertise to support the adoption of rooftop solar across manufacturing facilities, automotive companies, warehouses, FMCG, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, educational institutions, and households.
items.title: Moglix Launches End-to-End Rooftop Solar Business Targeting Industrial, Commercial, and Residential Customers

items.summary: According to the Globe and Mail, citing unnamed sources, Canada's Enbridge is reportedly negotiating with a group of Indigenous communities over the sale of a 6% stake in its Line 3 pipeline network. The deal could fetch more than C$1.5 billion (over $1 billion), which would make it the largest transaction involving Indigenous communities in the country. Line 3 has a capacity of roughly 760,000 barrels of crude daily and links Alberta's oil sands to Wisconsin; Enbridge's broader pipeline network can carry up to 3.2 million barrels per day. In response to a request for comment, an Enbridge spokesman said the company is
items.title: Enbridge in Talks to Sell a 6% Line 3 Stake for Over $1 Billion

items.summary: Standard & Poor's placed Nvidia's AA credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade on Wednesday (Nov. 25), warning it could lower the rating within 90 days but expecting any change to be limited to one notch unless investigations and disclosures harm the company's reputation or prospects. S&P cited weaknesses in management and board oversight, noting that certain long-tenured board members may have compromised their independence and that governance practices had not kept pace with Nvidia's rapid growth as a critical global technology enabler. The move follows a turbulent leadership period after CEO Jensen Huang resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs involving his direct reports and Alice Huang—a Chinese businesswoman alleged by U.S. intelligence to be Beijing's spy—before the board reinstated him on Monday, attributing the return to U.S. government input while an independent committee continued its investigation. Investors were largely unruffled: Nvidia shares fell nearly 4 percent Wednesday after dropping about 38 percent since Oct. 6 and following a Nasdaq 100 index that briefly flirted with a 20 percent decline from its recent high, though the five-year credit default swap spread for Nvidia was little changed.
items.title: S&P Puts Nvidia on Downgrade Watch Amid Leadership Turmoil

items.summary: The UK's competition watchdog, the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), has called for a shake-up of the £8bn private dentistry market after an investigation identified what it described as a 'catalogue of concerns,' including inflation-busting annual price rises and evidence of targets to sell more expensive treatments. The CMA found that prices rose by an estimated 7% a year on average between 2023 and 2025 at large dental groups, well ahead of inflation and wage growth. This is particularly acute in certain regions: a composite white filling makes up around 36% of mean weekly disposable income in the North East of England and 35% in Wales. The watchdog said patients faced substantial price differences across different parts of the UK and that commercial practices, targets and incentives may not operate in their best interests; dentists typically have a financial stake in treatment revenues as practice owners or through revenue-sharing arrangements. It also found significant variation even within the same area: online prices for composite fillings ranged from £80 to £223 in Preston, while amalgam filling prices ranged from £72 to £159 in Caerphilly. The CMA said about 60% of patients across the UK now pay for at least some private dental care, including many on low incomes, but it is difficult for them to confidently shop around and get a good deal; one in six private practices does not publish price lists online, and there was substantial variation in indicative profit margins. The proposed measures would make it easier to compare and switch through clearer treatment plans, better access to dental records and diagnostic information, and a new online source of NHS and private dentistry information; increase workforce capacity via expanded domestic training, fuller use of dental therapists and hygienists, and fewer barriers for overseas-qualified professionals; strengthen consumer protection with clearer accountability and complaints arrangements; and enable governments to more directly shape the market using their significant NHS buying power. A separate study by Zental Dental found that dental care is the medical treatment Brits most often delay or skip for financial reasons, with prices up 29% since 2021 (a private check-up now costs £55). The research examined 16 treatments and read 7,589 posts in 54 UK forum threads; dental care ranked first among delayed treatments. Out of every 100 people posting about their dental care, 14 said price had led them to delay or go without treatment, with going less often the most common response ahead of not affording a visit. When listing cutbacks made to cope with cost of living, 76 named dental care unprompted.
items.title: UK Competition Watchdog Calls for Shake-up of £8bn Private Dentistry Market

items.summary: According to a report by the Financial Times on Thursday (November 26), Nvidia instructed its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to four Southeast Asian countries. The reporting cited three people with knowledge of the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
items.title: Nvidia Halts Chip Shipments to Southeast Asia, FT Reports

items.summary: On Monday, Wipro led a rally among technology stocks, with Infosys, HCL Technologies, LTTS, and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) also advancing amid strong market momentum and the reversal of the AI trade. The gains in IT stocks occurred even as the rupee appreciated 3-6 percent against key currencies, which threatens to pressure IT margins at a time when weak growth and pricing pressures have reduced the sector's ability to absorb foreign exchange shocks.
items.title: Wipro Leads IT Stock Rally as Rupee Appreciation Threatens Margins

items.summary: American restaurant chain Denny's sent an emotional message to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on X, writing 'Jensen, your seat is waiting for you and the coffee is ready,' following a dispute over a commemorative plaque. The plaque at Denny's in Berryessa Drive, San Jose—where Huang and his co-founders reportedly discussed what became of Nvidia—had originally read that the company began from this very seat and went on to become worth $100 billion (one lakh crore dollars). In 2023 the chain had placed a plaque near the specific seat where the founding conversation occurred. The plaque was later removed, sparking controversy; Denny's said it wrote to Nvidia's communications team on November 10 stating that both Jensen and the restaurant are part of each other's history, then received notice on November 13 that the plaque had been taken down, after which it was reinstalled. Denny's did not disclose who removed the plaque or why. Huang reportedly worked washing dishes and serving customers at this same restaurant before his tech career, still considers these early days formative, and views the location as part of his story.
items.title: Denny's Restores Nvidia-Founding Plaque After Jensen Huang Reaches Out

items.summary: A West Sussex soup kitchen has warned that many families are likely to cut back on essentials during the festive period as they try to cover holiday expenses. Katrina McCormack, chief executive of the Shout Worthing Soup Kitchen, told BBC Radio Sussex that high demand at Christmas forces them to limit support and keep shelves stocked, with some people now asking for help they would not need in other months—such as families requesting an air fryer because they cannot afford to run a cooker. The charity is also running a campaign to raise funds for turkey and other Christmas items for struggling families. New research from Save the Children found that 65% of parents of children under 16 in the UK were concerned about affording Christmas, with nearly a third planning to buy fewer presents than usual and 16% intending to reduce heating use in December to save money. Separately, Nicky Chisholm of Brighton is aiming to fundraise enough to feed 500 people on Christmas Day through her online campaign that has run for 16 years.
items.title: Soup kitchen warns families will cut essentials at Christmas amid cost of living pressures

items.summary: U.S. District Court Judge Loren AliKhan issued a preliminary injunction blocking President Trump's administration from proceeding with reviews of the broadcast licenses of ABC and its parent company Walt Disney Co., ruling that the agency's early review was unconstitutional retaliation for speech the president disliked, including late-night jabs by Jimmy Kimmel, critical remarks on The View, and moderation of a September 2024 presidential debate. Judge AliKhan relied heavily on public statements and social media posts in which Trump attacked ABC and Disney, counting eleven calls over two years to strip their licenses, with the most recent attributed to July 2026; she also cited FCC Chairman Brendan Carr as acting on those threats. The court found that because losing broadcast licenses is an existential penalty for a company serving six of the nation's largest markets — including New York, Los Angeles, and Houston — premature review creates enough risk to chill broadcasters of ordinary firmness. ABC called the ruling
items.title: Federal Judge Blocks FCC License Review of ABC and Disney, Citing Retaliation for Free Speech

items.summary: In an interview with Tyler Cowen, Moxie Marlinspike of Signal addressed whether artificial intelligence could undermine cryptography and privacy, arguing that the prevailing approach to AI safety is mass surveillance. He described this conventional method as classifying everyone's actions on a scale from most bad to least bad and having human reviewers evaluate all activity—an apparatus he characterized as larger and more efficient than any other in history, which he considers dangerous. Marlinspike offered his own alternative: surveilling the AI models themselves instead of the humans who use them, though he acknowledged that achieving privacy alongside accountability for agents remains a difficult challenge to navigate.
items.title: Marlinspike Argues for Surveillance of AI Models Rather Than Users

items.summary: Nvidia has instructed its manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to stop shipping servers containing its chips to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. According to three people with knowledge of the matter, Nvidia will not allow these orders to be shipped as it works out how to comply with new US export controls aimed at preventing Chinese access to advanced AI computing power. The four countries have become favored destinations for Chinese AI developers seeking workarounds around Washington's restrictions. Nvidia booked US$104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, a 72 per cent increase over the prior year according to company accounts, and also records some Taiwan and China revenue via that unit. The new controls follow rules introduced by the Commerce Department last week giving cloud providers a 90-day deadline to obtain licenses proving their end users are not restricted entities; one cloud provider executive described the lack of execution guidance as causing
items.title: Nvidia Halts Chip Shipments to Four Southeast Asian Countries Over US Export Controls

items.summary: Days after President Donald Trump declared Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang not a security threat to the United States, senior U.S. national security officials at the White House, FBI, and CIA have debated whether his former business associate, Alice Huang—a former executive at a major Nvidia customer—was working for or passing information to China's Ministry of State Security (MSS). According to five anonymous sources familiar with the matter, these officials are trying to determine if she was acting as an agent. Two of those people said the U.S. has collected intelligence on Alice Huang and her contact with individuals associated with the MSS, describing this intelligence for months in reports from several agencies including the CIA.
items.title: U.S. Officials Divided Over Whether Alice Huang Was a Chinese Spy

items.summary: Southeast Asia is emerging as an offshore hub through which Chinese companies access advanced US chips that are otherwise restricted for export to China. Malaysia has received €510 billion ($559 billion) in AI infrastructure investment since February 2025, and the consulting group Fitch Solutions counts 125 data centers there, with 16 of 27 new sites located in Johor; Kuala Lumpur expects up to 90% of resulting jobs filled by locals. Major US firms have also invested heavily along the Strait of Malacca: Amazon and Oracle each $6 billion, Microsoft and Google $2 billion apiece, plus Alphabet's additional $15 billion announced in early November. Chinese companies are circumventing export controls by legally purchasing or leasing overseas data center capacity to rent access to US chips installed there and develop AI models abroad; the Washington-based Institute for Progress estimated that about 24% of China's total computing power came from remote access to overseas data centers (three-quarters in Southeast Asia), a share predicted to rise to 31% by end of 2027, though it noted these figures are difficult to size because cloud providers and developers rarely disclose customers or capacity. Alibaba Cloud operates six Malaysian data centers as part of $53 billion invested globally, while Tencent signed a five-year $7 billion Oracle contract for computing equivalent to 100,000 modern AI chips (with 30% payment due upfront) before the deal reportedly collapsed amid Beijing and Washington pressure.
items.title: Chinese Firms Route AI Compute Through Southeast Asia Amid Chip Sanctions

items.summary: Japan has protested to the United States over plans to impose a 15% levy on Japanese imports in response to alleged manufacturing excess capacity, according to Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara at a Thursday news conference — even though that rate matches what the two countries agreed upon last year. The U.S. announced Wednesday it intends to apply the 15% tariff while leaving open the possibility of raising it to 20%, both levels consistent with the prior agreement under which President Donald Trump set tariffs at 15% on Japanese products and lower duties on automobiles in exchange for a $550 billion Japanese investment initiative. Kihara denied that Japan has any nonmarket policies or structural excess production capacity, calling the measures regrettable while affirming continued cooperation on the steadily implemented program, which so far includes three rounds of projects worth $130 billion — progress described as smoother than similar deals with countries such as South Korea.
items.title: Japan protests U.S. tariff plan, citing no excess capacity

items.summary: In Beijing on Wednesday, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called for joint efforts with the Netherlands to keep industrial and supply chains stable and unobstructed. The remarks came during a meeting between Ding—a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee—and Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen. Ding characterized the two countries' relationship as an open, pragmatic partnership for comprehensive cooperation that leads all China-EU ties, and noted that next year marks the 55th anniversary of their ambassadorial diplomatic relations; he said China is ready to implement the consensus reached by their heads of state, deepen cross-sector exchanges, and promote steady bilateral growth. Ding also urged both major economies to work together for shared national and global growth. Berendsen congratulated China on hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, praised its development achievements, and said the Netherlands is ready to strengthen high-level exchanges with China, expand practical cooperation across all fields, resolve differences through dialogue, and pursue common prosperity.
items.title: Chinese Vice Premier Urges Netherlands to Stabilize Supply Chains

items.summary: Global markets rebounded Thursday after a dip-buying afternoon rally lifted US stocks off their initial lows ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, while Asian tech shares led gains and investors absorbed fresh proposed US tariffs. Beaten-down Asian technology firms drove the recovery, with Japanese chipmaker Kioxia and investment giant SoftBank surging by double figures, alongside South Korean SK hynix and Samsung; Tokyo's Nikkei 225, Seoul's Kospi, Taipei's Taiex, Hong Kong's Hang Seng, plus Sydney, Shanghai and Singapore all climbed more than 1%, while Wellington and Manila dipped. The gains followed a volatile week in which news of Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia lit up Asian screens Tuesday before a sharp drop Wednesday as the AI-boom euphoria faded amid concerns over capital expenditure, rising interest rate expectations and tighter regulation talk under a new Democrat-led Congress. Forex.com's Michael Boutros cautioned that buyers still need to show renewed demand extends beyond short-lived relief rallies, with December focus on whether semiconductor shares can support a broader recovery or signal further downside. Separately, US inflation data at a three-year high boosted expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month after third-quarter growth was revised up. Proposed tariffs on 14 economies following an investigation into alleged excess production drew little market reaction; duties of up to 20% face public comment before taking effect and target the EU, India, Japan, South Korea and China — which faces a joint-highest 20% toll that US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said stays within existing trade negotiations.
items.title: Asian Tech Stocks Rebound as Tariff Fears Ease

items.summary: Children's hospitals in England are closing beds and reducing staff as they struggle to meet cost-cutting targets set by NHS chiefs. Great Ormond Street Hospital has closed 28 beds, shut its Hedgehog ward (10 beds), reduced several other wards, and is cutting 300 posts while seeking £50.6m in savings by the end of March; two-thirds of its £31.5m cost improvement programme for 2026/27 will come from workforce reductions. Sheffield children's hospital has closed eight surgical beds due to falling demand and is cutting 300 of its 3,500 full-time equivalent staff to save £17.7m this year (about 5% of budget). Alder Hey in Liverpool must save around £24m before next April; it halved ward 4C beds from 32 to 16 and is reducing its 4,000-strong workforce while also cutting 300 posts. Sheffield and Alder Hey have rated their financial difficulties a major risk of 20 out of 25 in their latest registers. The Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health warned the cuts could limit hospitals' ability to cope with winter surges, while NHS England said children's services remain a priority.
items.title: UK Children's Hospitals Close Beds and Cut Staff to Meet NHS Cost-Cutting Targets

items.summary: Severe disruption is expected across the London Underground on Thursday and Friday as RMT tube drivers begin a 24-hour strike starting at noon Thursday, marking the first action in a fresh wave of strikes over the planned introduction of a four-day working week. Talks to prevent the dispute ended without resolution at Acas conciliation on Tuesday. The union has scheduled seven more stoppages, including two 24-hour closures before Christmas that would affect transport during some of the capital's busiest shopping days; RMT's next dates are Thursday and Saturday December 17-19, with further strikes planned for January 4 and 6 (noted as 2027 in the source) plus three more in February. The union represents just under half of tube drivers and claims the working-pattern changes were being imposed at risk to safety, while London Underground said they are voluntary and argued that a four-day week would reduce annual hours spent at work while improving service reliability; rival union Aslef welcomed the proposal. TfL warned passengers to plan ahead, with most lines operating Thursday except Piccadilly and Circle (Waterloo & City closed from midday), reduced services across much of the network finishing early in the evening, no service after 9pm Friday, later starts around 7am on Friday, while Elizabeth line, London Overground, national rail, and buses remain open but crowded. Nick Dent of London Underground said the strike was disappointing and urged RMT to put its proposal to members; RMT general secretary Eddie Dempsey countered that drivers would be forced to give up protections regardless of whether they work four or five days and face depot displacement if they refuse.
items.title: RMT Tube Drivers Begin Four-Day Week Strike; More Stoppages Planned Through Christmas

items.summary: More than 800 people gathered Nov. 17-20 in Bruges, Belgium for the 7th World Conference on Marine Biodiversity (q1/q2), which addressed topics ranging from deep-sea mining impacts to ocean-related art and citizen science while raising broader questions about how society values marine ecosystems. David Obura of CORDIO East Africa opened with a keynote calling for a shift away from market-driven exploitation toward balance, sustainability, and long-term security over short-term gain (attributed). Many participants stressed the need to catalog overlooked or undescribed species; Bert Hoeksema of Naturalis Biodiversity Center said “there are so many species that are not known” (attributed). The conference occurred just after the midway point of the U.N. Ocean Decade, which runs 2021-2030 and was decided by the U.N. General Assembly in 2017; organizer Leen Vandepitte called it “an excellent moment to take stock” (attributed). Organized by VLIZ, whose World Register of Marine Species catalogs more than 250,000 known marine species maintained by about 350 taxonomists who add roughly 2,000 new descriptions each year, the event noted that total estimates range from 500,000 to 2 million (q7/q8/q9/q10/q11). Sessions covered overlooked organisms such as seafloor nematodes affected by a 2021 deep-sea mining trial in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone conducted by Global Sea Mineral Resources (d12), scientific methods like environmental DNA analysis, and concerns that traditional taxonomic expertise is being lost. The conference also screened the 2025 documentary How Deep is Your Love about a mission to the same zone (d13). A banner image showed a jellyfish possibly new to science photographed during a 2025 NOAA expedition in Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument near Hawai‘i (d14).
items.title: 7th World Conference on Marine Biodiversity Highlights Overlooked and Undiscovered Ocean Life

items.summary: In Uttarakhand, India, high-altitude women farmers are cultivating endangered medicinal herbs such as kutki (Picrorhiza kurroa) and sugandha bala to help revive species that were being overharvested from alpine meadows. Women perform most of the labor in this enterprise because men often migrate for work, earning money to support their families and children's education. Scientists note that Uttarakhand has diverse agro-climatic conditions, making mountain villages at about 2,500 to 3,000 m altitude suitable for cultivating high-altitude medicinal and aromatic plants (MAPs). India is home to 8,000 medicinal plant species, of which 140 have been prioritized for national cultivation support, while Uttarakhand has listed 38 such species. Globally, market demand for MAPs grew substantially with $4.2 billion in exports in 2023, though unsustainable harvesting and overexploitation continue to threaten many species. Through ex situ conservation strategies like the NGO Udyogini's program—which provides farmers with 2,000 free saplings per 1-naali plot (about 200 square meters)—saplings are distributed directly or through partner organizations across six regions of Uttarakhand. By 2022, this effort had brought over 172 acres [70 hectares] under conservation, according to Shivam Pandey of Udyogini. The model also addresses human-wildlife conflict by utilizing land that wild animals leave untouched and reintroducing rare species into degraded bugyals.
items.title: Women Farmers in Uttarakhand Cultivate Endangered Himalayan Medicinal Plants

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen in Beijing on Wednesday, November 26, urging the Netherlands to ensure a fair, transparent and predictable business environment for Chinese companies operating there. During their talks, which focused on expanding bilateral cooperation, Wang said China supports two-way investment between the countries and welcomes more Dutch businesses investing and operating in China. He emphasized that China regards Europe as an important pole in a multipolar world and has maintained continuity and stability in its policy toward the EU, while welcoming European strategic autonomy. On sensitive issues, Wang stated that the Taiwan question is one of China's core interests and expressed hope that the Netherlands would honor the one-China principle through concrete actions to safeguard bilateral relations' political foundation. Berendsen responded by affirming that the Dutch government adheres to the one-China policy and this position will not change, while noting that practical cooperation between the two countries continues to deepen across various fields. Both ministers expressed willingness for the Netherlands to play a constructive role in promoting sound China-Europe relations.
items.title: Wang Yi Calls for Fair Business Environment as China-Netherlands Ties Deepen

items.summary: Since the start of the year, Beijing has installed 48 cloud benches across 26 public spaces in seven districts. Each bench is made from recycled polypropylene — roughly 1,000 takeout containers per seat — and board benches are formed from crushed milk cartons with their aluminum and plastic layers removed. Every finished seat carries a sign identifying the source of its recycled materials and how much was used. These products support Beijing's circular-economy effort to link neighborhood drop-off points, transfer stations and sorting centers; that network now covers over 20 universities, parks and railway stations, plus more than 140 office buildings and 11,207 communities, while an online platform offers door-to-door pickups for old furniture and appliances. Liu Jie of the Beijing Municipal Commission of Urban Management said what matters is giving residents feedback on their sorting and letting them see recycled results in public spaces so that recycling continues to become resources. The city plans to add more benches alongside improved walking and cycling routes.
items.title: Beijing's recycled-material 'cloud benches' combine public seating with a circular-economy recycling push

items.summary: NSW rail unions had planned a week-long strike over an ongoing enterprise bargaining dispute, but the Fair Work Commission has delayed its decision on whether the industrial action can legally proceed. As a result of this delay and uncertainty surrounding the planned stoppages, many regional and interstate train services scheduled for Friday will be replaced by coaches or cancelled.
items.title: Fair Work Commission Delays Rail Strike Decision, Disrupting NSW Services

items.summary: French armed forces seized 3.3 tonnes (3,328 kg) of methamphetamine from a small unflagged oil tanker outside French Polynesia's maritime zone last Friday, bringing this year's total drug seizures by France's Pacific forces to more than 15 tonnes. The boarding team found 150 bales weighing 3.328 tonnes that tested positive for methamphetamine; the vessel was spotted near Clipperton Island and tracked for several weeks with assistance from international partners, including a US Coast Guard maritime patrol aircraft. French Pacific Command (CPP) and French Armed Forces in French Polynesia (FAPF) released the crew and flagged the vessel to international authorities after transporting the drugs to Tahiti for destruction. Associate professor Jose Sousa-Santos of the University of Canterbury's Pacific Regional Security Hub described the tanker as a 'mothership' designed to travel undetected before offloading cargo onto smaller craft such as narco-subs, noting that its location near Clipperton suggested it was closer to origin than destination and pointing to stronger French-US cooperation. Sousa-Santos also said recent large cocaine seizures have shifted the Australian drug market toward methamphetamine.
items.title: France Seizes 3.3 Tonnes of Meth From 'Mothership' Tanker in the Pacific

items.summary: European Union leaders met in Brussels on Thursday to try to bridge deep divisions over the bloc's long-term budget, which includes a proposed €45 billion ($49.4 billion) loan to keep Ukraine funded through 2027 (q1, d2). The meeting centered on the new joint budget for 2028-2034, financed mostly by the 27 member countries based on their economies and expected to amount to between 1% and 1.2% of the bloc's gross national income (q3, q4-q5), with European Council President António Costa proposing a version cutting about 10% off the original Commission plan (q6). The package foresees a €100 billion ($110 billion) envelope for Ukraine over seven years and the new €45 billion loan; it also contemplates an EU-wide digital services tax that could raise €5 billion ($5.5 billion) annually from online advertising and user data (q7-q8). The commission plans to fund loans on capital markets, with €20 billion ($22 billion) for the economy and €25 billion ($27 billion) for armed forces; this follows a loan of 90 billion euros ($99 billion) endorsed nearly a year ago that covered most Ukrainian government needs for two years (q9-q14). items.title: EU Leaders Face Showdown Over Ukraine Funding as Divisions Deepen

items.summary: The Polish financial supervisory authority (KNF) approved UniCredit's public takeover and exchange offer for Commerzbank on 26 November, completing the regulatory authorisation process that had already received clearance from the European Commission on 16 November and the US Federal Reserve. The KNF approval specifically concerns the indirect change of control of Commerzbank's operations in Poland, including mBank, which the German group holds a 69.1 per cent stake in; it is one of Poland's main banking institutions with around 5.9 million customers and operates in mortgages, investment, and payments. Banking rules require supervisory review because the acquisition entails UniCredit taking control of Commerzbank's Polish subsidiaries through qualified indirect holdings. The deal follows a mid-November agreement between UniCredit chief executive Andrea Orcel and the German government, which secured eight binding commitments covering Frankfurt as the base for German operations, retention of Commerzbank's stock listing and legal form, representation on the group's executive committee, appointment of German nationals to UniCredit's board when renewed in 2027, support for German small- and medium-sized enterprises (Mittelstand), capital allocation, decision-making autonomy for German operations, investment in training, digital technologies, and artificial intelligence, union dialogue, and protection of existing employee agreements. The question of the German state's stake remains open: Berlin holds about 13.3 per cent of Commerzbank's share capital through the SoFFin stabilisation fund, announced it would not tender its shares by June, and has not yet committed to an immediate sale while using its holding to monitor the transaction and verify UniCredit honours its commitments on governance, employment, and Germany's role in the group. With regulatory approvals complete, implementation can proceed: crediting of new shares to custodian banks is scheduled for 7 December 2026, and UniCredit has asked Commerzbank to call an extraordinary general meeting to elect a new board as part of defining future governance. For UniCredit, the transaction implies an estimated capital absorption of between 200 and 225 basis points of CET1 in return for a significant expected contribution to group profits.
items.title: UniCredit Secures Final Polish Approval for Commerzbank Takeover

items.summary: Despite China-US dialogue remaining open at the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Washington advanced its export controls around the summit: on November 15 it signed a Pax Silica declaration with nine partners, and on November 16 moved to restrict remote access to advanced computing via third-country data centers effective November 19. CGTN's He Jingyi argues that dialogue can open a channel but does not remove policy barriers; with cooperation and controls running side by side, firms must navigate both as the next line of restriction is drawn.
items.title: APEC Dialogue Coexists with New U.S. Export Controls on Advanced Computing

items.summary: Rassvet, a Russian satellite communications network developed by Bureau 1440 and nicknamed the 'Russian Starlink,' is being used for military communications over Ukraine after Russia lost access to SpaceX's Starlink following an early-2026 whitelist that deactivated terminals operated by Russian forces. According to Ukrainian military intelligence (HUR), reported via Reuters in November, Rassvet has been deployed to improve strike accuracy and support reconnaissance drones, though HUR spokesperson Andriy Yusov said the constellation is currently insufficient for uninterrupted coverage of Ukraine. Rocket analyst Georgiy Trishkin told DW that Russia aims to field a sovereign system of 292 satellites by end-2027; SpaceX reportedly launched its first two serial Rassvet satellites in March and July 2026, with up to 300 planned for the first phase versus Starlink's over 10,000. Trishkin said no one can currently match SpaceX's technological or production edge—SpaceX manufactures about 15,000 terminals per day—and that Bureau 1440's terminals are more expensive due to reliance on foreign components. Ukrainian expert Oleh Starikov noted Russia's broader satellite network grew from 102 satellites before the February 2022 invasion (per Roscosmos director Dmitry Rogozin) to nearly four times that number by September, and said Rassvet could fulfill its military mission if it keeps developing.
items.title: Russia's Rassvet Satellite Network Faces Starlink Gap in Ukraine War

items.summary: Khalifa Haftar, leader of the eastern half of divided Libya, met Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Wednesday for his first official visit to the country, marking a significant thaw in relations between the longtime rivals. The meeting followed years during which Turkey backed the Tripoli-based, UN-recognised government against Haftar's forces and its leader Erdogan described him as 'a mercenary' while accusing regional powers of funding him; Ankara has since sought to deepen ties with power brokers across both halves of Libya. A photograph released by Erdogan's office showed the president meeting Haftar and his delegation, including his son Saddam Haftar, whom officials describe as a presumed heir, though Erdogan's office did not provide details of the closed-door talks. Earlier meetings between Haftar and Turkey's foreign and energy ministers, intelligence chief, and military leaders focused on regional and international developments plus issues of mutual interest, with both sides exploring ways to strengthen cooperation across several sectors in service of shared interests. The visit comes three days after a Ukrainian attack on two Russian ships near Benghazi that sank the corvette Merkury; Haftar maintains close ties with Russia while Turkey has sought to mediate between Moscow and Kyiv since the start of the Ukraine war, and separately hosted talks in October between representatives of both Libyan governments as one of few countries maintaining ties with both camps.
items.title: Erdogan Welcomes Haftar to Ankara Amid Push to Strengthen Ties With Eastern Libya

items.summary: As foreign troops begin withdrawing from Somalia, analysts worry the government may struggle to defend itself against Islamist militants while managing political divisions ahead of its first direct elections in decades. The African Union mission supporting Somali security forces includes about 12,000 personnel, with Ugandan troops—the largest contingent—having begun withdrawal last month and expected to complete it by next year. Ethiopia, another major contributor with over 7,000 soldiers, is reportedly planning to withdraw almost half of its force. Abdisalam Guleid, a former deputy director of Somalia's National Security Agency, warned that the withdrawals could leave Mogadishu vulnerable to an al-Shabab takeover similar to Afghanistan's fall in 2021 after US and NATO forces departed; he added that Ugandan troops have been central to preventing such a collapse since their first deployment in 2007. Somalia's Information Minister Abdifatah Qasim Mohamud rejected concerns, saying Somali troops had already taken over vacated positions. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud sought continued international backing during an 23 November visit to Uganda. Analysts also flagged a worsening security picture: al-Shabab claimed to have killed hundreds of elite soldiers in a recent attack the government acknowledged without disclosing casualties; clan militias aligned with rival factions are challenging the federal government, including loyalists fighting alongside al-Shabab; and forces loyal to ousted regional President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed are battling the government in the Bay region. The timing is further complicated by an electoral dispute: constitutional amendments extending the presidential term from four to five years would have delayed elections until 2027, but this month's Supreme Court ruling ordered leaders to agree on a roadmap within 30 days and hold elections within three months—a decision Somalia rejects after President Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Baashe Yusuf Ahmed. On finances, donor grants of $878.8m make up two-thirds of Somalia's planned $1.36bn budget for 2026, though the ministry reported receiving only about $314m in the first nine months—roughly 35% of expected annual aid. Guleid is skeptical that partners such as Turkey, Qatar and Egypt could quickly replace Uganda and the US militarily and financially.
items.title: Somalia's Foreign Troop Withdrawals Raise Questions Over Its Ability to Defend Against al-Shabab

items.summary: Nigeria's opposition is accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of orchestrating attacks against presidential candidate Peter Obi during campaign rallies nationwide. On Wednesday, a gunman opened fire on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City. NDC National Chairman Cleopas Moses said at a press conference in Abuja that despite legitimate communication and without even holding a full swing campaign, Obi's town-hall meeting had been under attack from the airport since morning. Last year, Edo state governor publicly warned Obi that his safety would not be guaranteed if he came to the region. The NDC linked Wednesday's attack to a recent deadly event in Delta State and other incidents during Obi's campaign in Cross River and Lagos. Moses told reporters that the attacks had become too numerous, stating it is clear these are coordinated, deliberate efforts to silence the NDC and its candidates. Despite the violence, Obi continued with his town hall meeting where he urged Nigerians to defend their votes; he is scheduled to continue campaigning in Abia state. President Bola Tinubu is running for a second term in January's election against 17 other presidential candidates, including Obi and Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress.
items.title: Nigeria Opposition Accuses Ruling APC of Attacks on Peter Obi

items.summary:
The article argues that the global jihadist movement has failed to achieve its core goal of seizing territory and ruling by strict Islamic law, but is instead changing tactics rather than disappearing. Neither al-Qaeda nor IS reached this objective: IS lost its last territorial stronghold in 2019 after once controlling large areas of Iraq and Syria, while al-Qaeda never held comparable ground. Instead, the movement's center of gravity has shifted to Africa, where branches such as JNIM (in Mali) and al-Shabab (in Somalia), plus IS affiliates across Nigeria, the DRC, the Sahel, Mozambique and Somalia, are fighting long-running insurgencies.

A growing debate within jihadism pits hardliners against pragmatists. Hardliners reject compromise—holding back from imposing strict Islamic law, accepting man-made laws or constitutions, taking part in elections, working with non-Islamist groups, or building ties with governments they consider infidel. Pragmatists see cooperation as a route to power. The movement's most visible pragmatist is Syria's Ahmed al-Sharaa (formerly Abu Mohammed al-Jolani), who rose to power there in December 2024 after breaking from IS and al-Qaeda, distancing himself from global jihad calls, building alliances with non-Islamists, reassuring Russia as he advanced on Damascus, and being welcomed by Western leaders including US President Donald Trump during a November 2025 White House visit. The Taliban's return to Afghanistan in 2021 is cited as another model showing an Islamist movement could eventually take control of a country.

Two groups are especially watched for how they handle this shift. JNIM joined forces with nationalist Tuareg separatists in late April and dropped al-Qaeda branding from its videos since late 2024, reframing itself around local grievances while promising security, justice and prosperity alongside Islamic law; Africa specialist Aman Bezreh says the rebranding is progressing more slowly because of territorial expansion. France 24 jihadism expert Wassim Nasr notes a leadership split between those favoring the Taliban's force-based approach and those closer to HTS-style compromise.

Al-Shabab appears willing to make deals too, having reached an October truce with the Ma'awisley tribe; BBC Monitoring Somalia specialist Abdullahi Guji says its withdrawal of fighters could weaken government campaigns as African Union forces withdraw from Somalia amid funding cuts. Analysts attribute emboldenment partly to perceived Western distraction over Ukraine, a US-Iran conflict and China-Russia rivalries.

The central question remains unresolved: whether this pragmatism is genuine change or what Soufan Center's Colin Clarke calls a 'Trojan horse strategy'—gaining power without abandoning the goal of establishing an Islamic state. History shows al-Qaeda has long shown flexibility, advising groups in Yemen, Libya and Tunisia to adopt local names like Ansar al-Sharia after 2011, and urging restraint in Mali in 2012 as strategic patience rather than giving up ambitions.

The article concludes that while the global jihadist dream may have failed, jihadism is far from finished. It remains too early to say whether groups like JNIM and al-Shabab will follow the Taliban or Syrian examples.
items.title: Jihadist Groups Are Shifting Toward Local Power and Pragmatism

items.summary: Apple announced Thursday that it will open its first store in Hyderabad, Apple Kukatpally at Lake Shore-Y Junction Mall, on December 10. items.summary: Apple removed Shanghai-based MiniMax's AI companion app Talkie from its App Store worldwide after ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism reported that the app's AI-generated characters sent sexualized and abusive messages to children. Launched in 2023, Talkie offers romantic companions for users to chat with and is popular in the US, the Philippines, and Mexico according to Sensor Tower. Although the app carries an 18+ rating on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store — where it says children under 14 or under 16 cannot sign up depending on country — child safety advocates have criticized its lax verification safeguards that let users self-report their age. Talkie and MiniMax's Chinese version, Xingye, contributed over 60% of MiniMax's income in 2024 before the company stopped breaking out chatbot-related revenue shares; it had roughly 11 million monthly active users across its app and website as of October 2026 according to Unique. The removal comes amid growing scrutiny of AI companions, which are designed for sustained emotional engagement rather than large-language-model assistants like ChatGPT or Gemini. Elon Musk's Grok was criticized after generating sexualized images of women and children, Character.AI faces several US lawsuits over inappropriate interactions with minors, and China cracked down on domestic companion apps in July by banning intimate relationships for minors and ordering stricter guardrails against emotional dependency and addiction — prompting ByteDance and Alibaba to disable humanlike interactive agents. MiniMax has since shifted focus toward enterprise coding and multimodal models such as M1 and Hailuo-02 following its Hong Kong IPO in January, while Chinese users have pushed back against the regulatory efforts after forming attachments to virtual characters. Both Apple and MiniMax declined comment.
items.title: Apple Removes MiniMax's Talkie Chatbot From App Store Over Child Safety Concerns

items.summary: Following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's acknowledgment of an extramarital affair, Silicon Valley family lawyers are receiving increased inquiries from tech executives about prenuptial agreements to protect assets such as company shares. Fortune reported that some callers have directly cited the Nvidia scandal in their requests. Huang resigned on November 12 and was reinstated by the board on November 23; it remains unclear whether his wife, Lori Huang, will file for divorce after a 41-year marriage during which they reportedly had no prenuptial agreement. Monica Mazzei of Buchalter's San Francisco office told Fortune that requests for partner nondisclosure agreements represent a new trend alongside rising demand for prenups. Libby Leffler, founder and CEO of the online prenup service ThisFirst, said more clients are pointing to tech executives when requesting agreements, with many being founders or early employees at companies not yet public who want to decide in advance how shares or stock options would be treated if a marriage ends; she also noted that some clients reference Jeff Bezos's reported prenuptial agreement. Mazzei could not directly tie the surge in requests from Anthropic employees following its November 19 $1.5 trillion valuation to the Nvidia scandal, noting instead that prenups were already becoming more common among younger clients.
items.title: Silicon Valley CEOs Seek Prenups and Partner NDAs After Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: Elon Musk pledged on Wednesday that every child in the US will receive two shares of SpaceX — one newly issued share from the company and one donated personally by him — a gift he valued at some $18 billion. The pledge comes as Musk, described here as the world's richest person with a net worth around $824 billion, frames giving equity directly to people as his approach; most of his philanthropy reportedly flows through the Musk Foundation, which holds more than $14 billion in assets. SpaceX said it would contribute one newly issued Class A share to every currently active Trump Account and that Musk will personally match each company donation. The personal shares from Musk are set to transfer when his lockup expires in June next year, while the company's shares were slated for transfer next month; a separate post announced the transfers. SpaceX shares closed at $127.44 on Wednesday, valuing the pledge at nearly $18 billion, and Musk held about 6.42 billion SpaceX shares as of June. The White House said in October it had opened almost 70 million Trump Accounts for Americans under 18.
items.title: Musk Pledges Two SpaceX Shares Per American Child, Valuing Gift at $18 Billion

items.summary: Vice President JD Vance told New York Insight that federal officials assured him Jensen Huang was under no investigation when the White House sought his reinstatement to Nvidia. According to Vance, he received this assurance from the Department of Justice and multiple national security officials, including Attorney General Todd Blanche, who stated Huang faced not even a pending prosecution. Vance said he had seen no evidence that Huang committed a crime and argued that accusations based on anonymous reporting in The New York Times should not cause people to lose their jobs. He framed the situation as an opportunity for Nvidia to improve its compliance with American export controls while emphasizing that the decision to reinstate Huang rested with the company's board, though sources have reported President Trump asked him to help secure Huang's return. Vance's comments concern only Jensen Huang personally and not the broader investigations surrounding his wife Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed International accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to China; she is being examined in two Justice Department probes into chip diversion involving Megaspeed and Super Micro, while US intelligence agencies continue examining whether her relationship with Jensen Huang influenced alleged smuggling. In a classified briefing on Tuesday, officials told congressional staffers there was no evidence Chinese intelligence directed Alice Huang to spy on Jensen Huang, though they noted China's Ministry of State Security had approached her for information and that assessments could change.
items.title: Vance Says Officials Assured Him Jensen Huang Was Under No Investigation

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India repatriated 60.08 tonnes of gold from overseas custodians during the six months ended September 2026 (q1), raising domestically held gold to 740.13 tonnes in September from 680.05 tonnes at end-March (q3, q4). As a result, the share of India's total gold reserves stored within the country rose to about 84% from 77.23% six months earlier (q5, q6), while overall holdings stayed flat at 880.52 tonnes and overseas-held gold fell to 140.39 tonnes (q7, q8). The valuation of India's gold reserves declined to $106.08 billion from $115.40 billion in March, the RBI said this was mainly due to falling international gold prices (q9, q10). Separately, total foreign exchange reserves climbed to $737.78 billion at end-September from $691.11 billion in March, an increase of $46.67 billion (q11, q12, q13), with foreign currency assets rising to $608.26 billion from $552.28 billion over the period (q14, q15). The RBI also raised its proportion of foreign currency assets invested in securities to 87.06% from 84.31%, while cutting exposure to deposits with overseas central banks and the BIS (q16, q17).
items.title: RBI Repatriates 60 Tonnes of Gold, India Now Holds 84% of Its Bullion Domestically

items.summary: The United States proposed a tariff of up to 25 percent on Indian goods, which the USTR said could fall to 17 percent if New Delhi reaches a trade deal with Washington. This proposal sits at the top end of India's tariff range since April 2025, when Trump's 'Liberation Day' exercise imposed a combined 26 percent duty (a 10 percent baseline plus a 16 percent reciprocal component). The rate climbed to 50 percent in August after an additional penalty was added for Indian purchases of Russian oil. In February 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled that IEEPA did not authorize Trump's 'Liberation Day' tariffs; afterward he imposed fresh Section 122 duties and later a Section 301 tariff citing forced-labour concerns. The current proposed rate is separate from the existing 10 percent duty Indian exporters have paid since July, while India says it has no structural excess capacity in any sector.

items.summary: A new book by Prakash Iyer recounts how Alan Mulally's leadership of Ford Motor Company during its 2006-2008 downturn turned on one honest conversation. When Mulally, a Boeing executive who had spent his career building aircraft, began holding weekly 'business plan review' meetings where leaders presented updates using green (on track), yellow (caution), and red (trouble) color codes, he was struck by an unbroken sea of green slides despite the company losing billions. At that first meeting Mulally stopped proceedings to ask why nothing seemed wrong given Ford's financial losses, finding that admitting trouble had become a career risk in the culture where 'the messenger got shot long before the message was heard.' The turning point came when Mark Fields, head of Ford's Americas business, presented a red slide about a faulty part threatening to delay the launch of the Ford Edge after colleagues reportedly shifted their chairs away from him; Mulally clapped and called it 'great visibility,' then asked who could help solve the problem. This intervention saved the vehicle launch and kept Fields in his job, with Fields later succeeding Mulally as chief executive. The following week's meeting showed a rainbow of colors for the first time, which Mulally identified as the moment he knew Ford would survive—becoming the only major American carmaker to avoid a government bailout through the 2008 crisis—because his team was finally working on reality rather than 'beautifully formatted fiction.' Iyer frames this episode around the metaphor of the 'watermelon dashboard,' an item that appears green outside but is red throughout, arguing that organizations everywhere have such moments when projects report success until they slip and teams stay engaged until members resign. The author contends that leaders shape what their team reports by applauding or frowning at slides: rewarding only good news yields only good news while punishing red slides drives problems underground where they grow into disasters, so a leader's first job is to make it safe for people to tell the whole truth.
items.title: How a red slide saved Ford amid the 2008 financial crisis

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh authorities busted an alleged adulterated paneer manufacturing unit in Aghaura village, Raebareli district, on Monday night during the wedding season. The Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) raid allegedly found Ranipal optical whitener—a laundry-product chemical—along with refined palmolein oil, citric acid, and caustic soda being used to make paneer under unhygienic conditions. An FIR was registered against owner Dhirendra Paswan and six workers under Sections 264 and 265 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Assistant Commissioner Vineet Kumar Pandey said officials collected samples of all chemicals used, plus milk and paneer; around 1,500 litres of milk and over three quintals of paneer were destroyed. Samples will undergo laboratory testing to determine the extent of adulteration. Pandey warned that non-food-grade optical whiteners may cause gastrointestinal irritation, nausea and vomiting depending on chemical composition and concentration, while caustic soda can cause severe burns if consumed in high concentrations; he also noted permitted ingredients like citric acid and palmolein could constitute adulteration when used to pass off a product as genuine dairy paneer. Separately, earlier this month the FSDA Department in Mathura intercepted 2,500 kg of contaminated and suspicious paneer being brought into the border district from Rajasthan; officials destroyed the entire consignment, sent samples for testing, and arrested the transporting driver. Assistant Commissioner (Food) Jatin Kumar Singh attributed both incidents to elevated demand for khoya and paneer during the Diwali season, which he said is driving large quantities of substandard products across state borders.
items.title: UP FSDA raids alleged adulterated paneer unit amid wedding-season demand

items.summary: The Supreme Court told employees of the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) that there was "nothing much" it could do about their challenge to changes in their pension arrangements, because the Union government had approved selling a 60.7% stake in the bank to Canadian company Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited, per Live Law's report on Thursday. On October 14, the Ministry of Finance announced that the government and Life Insurance Corporation would sell their combined 60.7% stake for Rs 52,878 crore to Fairfax; the move followed RBI-imposed restrictions and a Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approval of IDBI's strategic restructuring after repeated capital infusions from the Government of India and LIC. The All India IDBI Officers Association had first approached the Bombay High Court challenging an April 18, 2012 bank circular that closed off another chance to join the Defined Benefit Pension Scheme, as well as retrospective salary deductions for New Pension Scheme contributions dating back to April 1, 2008. The High Court dismissed those appeals on the ground that IDBI Bank could not be treated as "state" under Article 12 of the Constitution; the Supreme Court agreed with that reasoning but allowed employees to pursue other legal remedies before an appropriate forum.
items.title: Supreme Court Finds It Can Do 'Nothing Much' on IDBI Staff Pension Challenge

items.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, speaking at a Constitution Day function organized by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) on November 26, said that public confidence in judicial authority must be continuously earned through independence, fairness, and consistency. He emphasized that disagreement is not a weakness of constitutional democracy and that a confident institution must engage with criticism without treating every disagreement as a challenge to its authority—provided such engagement remains guided by reasons, professional integrity, and respect for institutional processes. The CJI noted that the Constitution is tested daily in the ordinary exercise of power rather than only during extraordinary crises, judging it ultimately by what it means to the people it governs. He also highlighted ongoing challenges facing justice delivery—including pendency, delays, and unequal access to legal representation—stating that improving this situation is a shared responsibility requiring courts to strengthen processes for accessible justice while the Bar contributes through focused advocacy, responsible case management, and professional discipline. On training, the CJI assured SCBA members that a structured program would be introduced in a short time. Attorney General R Venkataramani added that efforts to improve administration of justice must not involve denigrating justice institutions or undermining judicial independence by mindlessly challenging it, warning that seemingly independent partisan considerations can invisibly impair the court's ability to function without fear or favour.
items.title: CJI: Public Confidence in Judicial Authority Must Be Continuously Earned Through Independence

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah marked the anniversary of the November 26, 2008 Mumbai terror attacks by paying tribute to the victims and security personnel killed. Speaking on Thursday via news agency Press Trust of India, he asserted that terrorism is 'the most heinous crime against humanity' and claimed India's zero-tolerance policy against terror was being praised worldwide while the country leads the global fight against terrorism. On X, Shah saluted soldiers who gave a 'crushing response' to terrorists and paid tribute to civilians killed in the attacks. The 2008 attacks were carried out by 10 heavily armed Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists from Pakistan across crowded locations including Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Trident Hotel, Nariman House, Leopold Cafe and Cama and Albless Hospital. The coordinated attacks left 166 people dead and more than 300 injured; Shah's remarks reiterated the government's zero-tolerance stance against terrorism.
items.title: Amit Shah Marks 26/11 Anniversary, Calls Terrorism the Most Heinous Crime Against Humanity

items.summary: Moshe Holtzberg, known as 'Baby Moshe,' who was two years old when footage of him crying after the November 26, 2008 Nariman House terror attack drew global attention and whose parents Rabbi Gavriel and Rivka Holtzberg were killed in the siege, is now pursuing rabbinical studies in New York with hopes of becoming a rabbi like his father. News agency Press Trust of India reported that he met two weeks ago at a rabbinical conference attended by 4,000 to 5,000 rabbis from across the world and was shown posing in traditional attire with fellow rabbis; Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky, who has overseen Nariman House activities since 2012, said Moshe now lives in Israel with his grandparents. Meanwhile, Mumbai's Nariman House is undergoing renovation: three of its six floors plus the ground floor will become a museum and memorial for attack victims while the remaining three floors continue Chabad House activities, with fundraising underway and completion expected within about 18 months.
items.title: Baby Moshe, survivor of the 2008 Mumbai attack, pursues rabbinical studies in New York

items.summary: Siemens Energy's shares rallied about 6% after the company reported a strong fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, with net profit jumping 82% year-on-year to Rs 653 crore from Rs 360 crore. Revenue rose 30.5% to Rs 3,453 crore from Rs 2,646 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA climbed 72% to Rs 822 crore against Rs 479 crore in the same period last year. The EBITDA margin expanded to 23.8% from 18.1%. These results lifted investor sentiment, prompting the rally as the Mumbai-based company hit an intraday high of Rs 3,231.60 on Thursday and traded at around Rs 3,135 by 9:40 am. Alongside its quarterly results, Siemens Energy announced a dividend of Rs 12 per equity share (face value Rs 2 each) for the financial year ended September 30, 2026, meaning an investor holding 100 shares could receive up to Rs 1,200.
items.title: Siemens Energy shares rally on strong Q4 FY26 earnings and dividend

items.summary: The Centre informed the Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 26) that a Look Out Circular (LOC) was issued against Saurav Das, co-convener of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), by Mumbai Police on November 23. The disclosure came during hearings into a plea filed after Das was stopped at Delhi airport from flying to Oxford University in the UK for an event on the 'cockroach movement.' Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice and set December 9 for further hearing, with the Centre's counsel noting that a show-cause notice had also been sent but not yet responded to. Das's lawyer stated he was unaware of any LOC, its purpose, or why it was issued. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke attributed the preventive measure to government jealousy toward the 27-year-old leader and alleged broader efforts by authorities to 'crush voices against' them, while asserting that India's Constitution remains on their side.
items.title: Centre Issues Look Out Circular Against Saurav Das as He Challenges UK Travel Ban

items.summary: The Information and Broadcasting ministry has asked Netflix to ensure that its first Pakistani show, 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo,' is not streamed in India. The request follows several complaints the ministry received about a possible December 4 release of the series, which reunites Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and Sanam Saeed and adapts Farhat Ishtiaq's 2013 Urdu novel 'All the Love Our Hearts Carry.' Netflix has not yet clarified whether its trailer dropped on Tuesday includes India in the show's availability. The ministry asked Netflix to adhere to an advisory dated May 8, 2025, which instructed streaming services to discontinue Pakistani-origin content after last year's Pahalgam terror attack, and to maintain a commitment it made in June that no film or series originating in Pakistan would be available to Indian subscribers. Two cine worker bodies—the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE)—have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi asking for a ban, calling the show's release a violation of the advisory; AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta described Pakistan as a 'terrorist country,' while FWICE president B N Tiwari warned it would halt all Netflix shoots if the series is released in India. In response, Pakistan's Planning and Development Minister Ahsan Iqbal used the hashtag #GrowUpIndia to push back against what he called weaponising art and culture.
items.title: India Ministry Asks Netflix to Keep Pakistani Show Off Indian Platform

items.summary: Following a direction from the Karnataka government, the Karnataka Co-operative Milk Producers' Federation Ltd. (KMF) reduced the selling price of Nandini curd by ₹2 per kg, with revised rates taking effect on November 29 in what KMF described as being in the interest of consumers. Under the new pricing, a 500 g pack that had cost ₹34 will now be priced at ₹33, and a 1 kg pack that was ₹68 will drop to ₹66. The reduction follows an earlier price revision effective November 1, 2026, when KMF raised curd prices on producers' request—lifting the 1 kg pack from ₹54 to ₹68 and the 500 g pack from ₹28 to ₹34—which drew criticism from consumers, opposition leaders, and hotel associations. Separately, the Karnataka Cabinet had approved an ₹8 per litre increase in Nandini milk prices effective November 1.
items.title: Karnataka Cuts Nandini Curd Prices by ₹2/kg From November 29

items.summary: BSE shares rose over 2% after HDFC Securities raised its target price, citing stronger-than-industry options activity. According to the brokerage report cited by ETNow, BSE's premium average daily turnover in October jumped 53% month-on-month to Rs 355 billion (q1–q2), sitting about 20% above its pre-CAS Q1FY27 average (q3). This outpaced the broader industry, whose premium average daily turnover rose only 42% month-on-month in October (q4). BSE's options premium market share improved to 33.5% in October from 32% in Q2 FY27 (q5–q6), with its main competitor being the National Stock Exchange. HDFC Securities also raised EPS estimates for FY27-29 by 1.3%-1.9% (q7–q8), though these figures exclude potential upside from cash-market share gains or an options price hike. Separately, BSE's shares closed 0.4% higher on Wednesday at Rs 3,775.20 versus the prior session of Rs 3,757 (q9–q11), delivering roughly 12% returns over one month and nearly 45% year-to-date (q12–q13). BSE reported a 45% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 809 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 558 crore, though profits fell about 7% sequentially (q14–q17).
items.title: HDFC Securities Raises BSE Target Price as Turnover and Earnings Estimates Rise

items.summary: On Wednesday night, four people were shot dead after unidentified assailants opened fire on a dhaba in Rohtak, Haryana. Deputy Superintendent of Police Rishi Kant confirmed the deaths and stated that no one was injured while an FIR had been registered; the attackers fled the scene before police launched multiple teams to identify them. Asked whether gang rivalry could have triggered the shooting, DSP Kant said all possible angles were being examined but declined to confirm a motive, noting there is currently no footage of the incident available. In a separate case in Delhi, police arrested Satyendra alias Sikandar (also referred to as Satinder alias Kanta) after an exchange of fire with a police team in Sonia Vihar on Tuesday while tracking him following a firing at a bar on Panchkuian Road in Paharganj; the suspect was injured by a bullet to his leg and taken for treatment. Delhi Police described him as the prime suspect in the Paharganj case, and authorities confirmed that the Rohtak shooting and the Delhi incident are separate cases with investigations underway in both cities.
items.title: Four Shot Dead at Dhaba in Haryana's Rohtak; Suspect Arrested in Separate Delhi Firing

items.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar paid tribute to victims and security personnel killed in the November 2008 attacks, marking its 18th anniversary on Thursday (November 26) while reaffirming India's zero tolerance for terrorism. The attacks began on the night of November 26, 2008, when 10 terrorists from Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba entered Mumbai by sea and carried out coordinated assaults over four days at sites including the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, Oberoi-Trident Hotel, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Nariman House, Cama Hospital, Metro Cinema and Leopold Cafe. The violence killed 166 people and injured around 300 others. Security forces killed nine of the ten attackers; the sole survivor, Mohammad Ajmal Amir Kasab, was captured alive, sentenced to death in May 2010, and hanged at Yerawada Central Jail in Pune in November 2012.
items.title: Jaishankar Marks 18th Anniversary of the 26/11 Mumbai Attacks
